CHIEF COMPLAINT
Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 63-year-old female who had mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. She reports feeling better overall since the surgery, though she had a rough time before the procedure. She continues to experience some chest pains and shallow breathing that occurs with exertion, typically lasting only a few minutes before resolving. These episodes occur approximately a couple times per month. Patient notes that slowing down when symptoms occur helps, and she is able to resume activities afterward. She reports that episodes go away for a couple weeks at a time. She is managing her condition by learning what she can and cannot do and adjusting her activity level accordingly. She denies new symptoms. Patient has history of mitral regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, asthma, and recurrent chest discomfort with previous negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease. At previous follow-up on 9/17, patient was doing well from a cardiac standpoint.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies new symptoms. Reports occasional chest pains and shallow breathing with exertion that resolve with rest. Denies medication side effects except for initial irritability from atenolol, which has resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Status post mitral valve repair (8/3/2020), mitral regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, asthma, recurrent chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease.

MEDICATIONS
Coumadin 4 milligrams, Lasix 4 milligrams daily, Atenolol 50 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Head and neck: No JVD detected. Lungs: Reduced breath sounds with clear auscultation and percussion. Heart: Irregularly irregular rhythm, S1 slightly accentuated, no S3. Abdomen: Non-tender to palpation. Extremities: Trace peripheral edema. Feet: Non-tender.

RESULTS
ECG taken 12/26/2020 shows atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response and T-wave inversion anteriorly. No significant changes compared to previous study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient recovering well from mitral valve repair surgery. Heart valves working well. Atrial fibrillation well controlled with current medications. Continue current medications: Coumadin 4 mg, Lasix 4 mg daily, Atenolol 50 mg daily. Encourage patient to remain active. Follow-up appointment in 6 to 9 months.
